channel.title: PsyDigest — psychiatry literature digest
channel.description: Summaries of new psychiatric research and guidelines

item.title: European psychiatrists' approaches to the treatment of bipolar disorder.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The European Psychiatric Association (EPA) undertook a study to investigate treatment preferences of European psychiatrists towards Bipolar Disorder (BD), as part of the Ambassador programme series of surveys. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey among psychiatrists and psychiatry trainees from 40 European countries. The questionnaire contained clinical vignettes of different phases of BD including manic, rapid cycling, mixed, hypomanic, and depressive episodes, for both initial and subsequent treatment strategies.

item.title: The effects of telerehabilitation in patients with chronic low back pain: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: ObjectiveLow back pain (LBP) represents a predominant cause of rehabilitation needs worldwide. Telerehabilitation has the potential to improve health systems by decentralizing clinical services and expanding healthcare accessibility. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate the effectiveness of telerehabilitation compared to face-to-face (FtF) rehabilitation or minimal interventions (e.g.

item.title: [Artificial intelligence in child and adolescent psychiatry: A critical review of uses, evidence and relational stakes].
item.description: OBJECTIVES: To critically appraise the main current and emerging uses of artificial intelligence (AI) in child and adolescent psychiatry across three high-burden domains - autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and depression and suicide risk - and to examine the level of evidence, methodological limitations, and the ethical, safety and relational challenges specific to this population. METHODS: Critical review of the literature.

item.title: Efficacy of progressive muscle relaxation training in post-traumatic stress disorder after the Kahramanmaraş earthquake: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The February 6, 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake was one of Turkey's most devastating natural disasters, causing serious psychological issues, especially Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Although various treatments exist for PTSD, they can be costly and sometimes ineffective. Progressive Muscle Relaxation Training (PMRT) is a low‑cost, self‑administered technique with no side effects, but randomized controlled trials on its effectiveness for post‑earthquake PTSD remain very limited.

item.title: Consensus-based guidelines for emotional intelligence interventions for first-year higher education students: a Delphi study.
item.description: A successful transition to higher education (HE) is associated with cognitive, social, and emotional skills that help students navigate developmental, contextual, and academic challenges. Emotional Intelligence (EI) has been linked to psychological adjustment and academic functioning. However, few interventions targeting first-year students are guided by structured and theoretically coherent frameworks.

item.title: Semaglutide modulates explore/exploit decision-making in major depressive disorder: A randomized clinical trial.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Explore/exploit decision-making is a crucial component of motivated behavior. Explore/exploit behaviors are related to disparate cognitive and reward-related functions and have been implicated in multiple neuropsychiatric conditions, including major depressive disorder (MDD). Several mediators of explore/exploit decision-making have been proposed; metabolic mechanisms have been theorized to potentially affect its underlying processes.

item.title: Healthcare utilization and costs associated with dextromethorphan-bupropion versus selected other branded treatments for major depressive disorder: a US real-world study.
item.description: AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and costs among adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) initiating dextromethorphan-bupropion (AUVELITY) versus cariprazine, brexpiprazole, or esketamine. METHODS: Using Merative MarketScan Commercial and Medicare claims data (January 2021-March 2024), adults initiating dextromethorphan-bupropion or a selected branded comparator between January 2022 and March 2024 were identified and assigned to mutually exclusive treatment cohorts (index date = first prescription claim).

item.title: Translating Evidence for Early Intervention in Psychosis (TRANSLATE): Protocol for Evaluating the Implementation of Early Intervention in Psychosis in Low and Lower-Middle Income Countries (LMICs).
item.description: BACKGROUND: In high-income countries, early intervention in psychosis (EIP) services provide treatment for first episode psychosis (FEP) as early as possible, proven to effectively improve health outcomes. These services rarely exist in low- and lower-middle-income countries (LMICs). The TRANSLATE study aims to evaluate the implementation of the EIP services using the selected indicators and to develop a clinical tool to predict the risk of Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia (TRS) in patients with FEP.

item.title: Exploring the Feasibility of a Generic Early Intervention Programme for Emerging Personality Disorder in Adolescents: Guideline-Informed Treatment for Personality Disorders-Adolescent Version (GITPD-A).
item.description: The Guideline-Informed Treatment for Personality Disorders-Adolescent version (GITPD-A) is an accessible, general approach to treating personality disorders (PDs) in adolescents. This study assessed the feasibility of the intervention and of a multicentre research design, as a preliminary step towards larger, better-controlled trials. A one-group pretest-posttest design was used across five mental healthcare institutions. Eligible participants were adolescents aged 12-18 meeting threshold criteria for a PD under the DSM-5 alternative model.

item.title: Multimodal Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Relapse in Major Depressive Disorder.
item.description: IMPORTANCE: Early identification of patients at high risk of relapse is key to personalized preventive strategies in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, current predictive models do not adequately account for the multimodal factors contributing to MDD relapse and fail to provide clinically meaningful predictions. OBJECTIVE: To predict relapse within 2 years in patients with MDD by using a comprehensive machine learning pipeline that integrates an unprecedented set of multimodal data.

item.title: Suicide mortality among survivors of first primary thyroid cancer: a population-based competing risk analysis.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Thyroid cancer is associated with favorable survival, yet suicide risk during long-term survivorship remains incompletely characterized, particularly in the presence of competing mortality. METHODS: We identified 178,014 patients with first primary thyroid cancer from the SEER 17 database between 2000 and 2022. Suicide mortality was quantified using standardized mortality ratios. Risk factors were evaluated using cause-specific Cox models and Fine-Gray competing risk regression, with non-suicide deaths treated as competing events.

item.title: Outdated Product Labeling and Implications for Contemporary Standards of Care: The Example of Clozapine.
item.description: Discontinuation of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's clozapine risk evaluation and mitigation strategy program led to a package insert (PI) revision in June 2025. However, that PI update retained many elements that are inconsistent with modern clozapine prescribing, including rapid titration, twice-daily dosing at the start of therapy, and titration without regard to patient factors (e.g., ancestry, sex and gender, or smoking status). The revision also provided no guidance on monitoring for myocarditis or mitigating the primary causes of mortality-pneumonia and ileus.

item.title: Oxytocin selectively enhances the recognition of infant sadness in postpartum depression.
item.description: BackgroundLittle is known about the role of oxytocin in the processing of positive emotional infant cues in mothers with PPD.ObjectivesWe therefore examined whether intranasal oxytocin influences postpartum mothers' processing of positive infant emotional cues, both visual (facial expressions) and auditory (laughter), and intended caregiving responses.DesignThis double-blind randomized controlled crossover study included 45 mothers, with 3- to 9-month-old infants, who exhibited clinically relevant scores on the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, with 35 mothers fulfilling the criteria of a […]

item.title: [Guideline for intervention and rehabilitation in children with autism spectrum disorder (2026 edition)].
item.description: On September 22, 2026, the National Health Commission released the "Guideline for intervention and rehabilitation in children with autism spectrum disorder (2026 edition)". The guideline applies to intervention and rehabilitation services for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) under 18 years of age.

item.title: Management of Patients on Medications for Opioid Use Disorder in the Perioperative or Peripartum Setting.
item.description: There is an increasing proportion of surgical and obstetric patients on medications for the treatment of opioid use disorder (medications for opioid use disorder [MOUD]), formerly known as medication-assisted treatment, in the United States. Due to lack of institutional protocols and limited evidence-based guidelines, perioperative management of patients on MOUD has largely been varied and often provider-dependent.

item.title: Breast carcinoma amplified sequence 2 rescues adult hippocampal neurogenesis and cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's disease via regulating BDNF/TrkB signaling.
item.description: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis (AHN) occurs throughout lifespan of humans and rodents and is correlated with memory performance and cognitive plasticity. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), AHN is impeded, while the molecular basis behind this impairment remains to be elucidated. Here we identified Breast carcinoma amplified sequence 2 (BCAS2), a core component of the CDC5L/Prp19 spliceosome complex, regulating AHN in AD.

item.title: Thalamocortical dysconnectivity shapes cortical hierarchy disruption across illness durations in schizophrenia.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Schizophrenia is increasingly conceptualized as a disorder of circuit-level dysfunction. However, how thalamocortical abnormalities differ across cohorts with varying illness durations and relate to large-scale cortical hierarchical organization remains unclear. METHODS: We analyzed resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from 1,223 patients with schizophrenia and 1,224 matched healthy controls across 12 datasets. The datasets were grouped as early-, middle-, and late-stage cohorts.

item.title: Brain NaV1.5 fine-tunes neuronal excitability to facilitate female-directed social behavior in male mice.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.5, an essential subtype for cardiac action potential generation, is also enriched in limbic regions of the brain, but its function in the central nervous system remains poorly understood. METHODS: We performed RNAscope, immunostaining, electrophysiology, fiber photometry, Scn5a knockdown, and behavioral testing to dissect the functional role of NaV1.5 in the brain. RESULTS: NaV1.5 channels are enriched in neurons of posterior bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNSTp) and accumulated at the axon initial segment.

item.title: Simultaneous measurement of Midbrain and Striatal Dopamine in Schizophrenia using an agonist radiotracer.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Imaging studies showing greater amphetamine-induced dopamine release in patients with schizophrenia (SCZ) compared to matched healthy controls (HC) have been repeatedly replicated, but these studies all used radiotracers that were dopamine D2 receptor antagonists. A more recent study using an agonist radiotracer did not detect this increase, raising a question whether the difference in radiotracer pharmacology affected the result.

item.title: Transdiagnostic factors differentially shape choices and decision times in social evaluative learning.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Learning from feedback provided by others is important for navigating complex social environments. Aberrant processing of such social feedback is implicated in the psychopathology of several mental health disorders including social anxiety and depression. Recent psychiatric research increasingly adopts transdiagnostic approaches that examine mechanisms and constructs cutting across traditional diagnostic categories. METHODS: Here, we applied reinforcement learning models together with transdiagnostic measures of psychopathology to formally assess social evaluation learning.

item.title: Public mental health: The case and required actions across the European region.
item.description: Despite the existence of effective public mental health (PMH) interventions, only a minority across the European region receive treatment for mental health conditions (MHCs). Even fewer receive interventions to prevent MHC-associated impacts, with negligible coverage of interventions to prevent MHCs, or promote mental well-being and resilience. Various reasons account for implementation failure which breaches the right to health and results in population scale preventable suffering, broad impacts and associated economic costs.

item.title: Coexistence of anhedonia and sensation-seeking with context-dependent gut dysbiosis in a prodromal transgenic mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
item.description: Accumulating evidence indicates that gut microbiota plays a role in the progression of Parkinson's disease (PD). Microbiota-based treatments for prodromal PD, which is accompanied by a wide range of neuropsychiatric symptoms, are being considered a potential early intervention but are still under-investigated. This study examined the association between symptoms of affective and motivational impairments and gut dysbiosis in a transgenic mouse model (line G2-3) that overexpresses A53T mutant α-synuclein, a key protein involved in the disease pathology.

item.title: Autism with social anxiety is associated with acquiescent behaviors and enlarged amygdala volume.
item.description: Social anxiety (SA) frequently co-occurs with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but it remains unclear whether SA in ASD reflects greater symptom severity or a distinct subtype. Across two complementary studies, we characterized the behavioral and neural correlates of SA in ASD using a naturalistic social navigation task measuring affiliative and power-related behaviors.

item.title: Lifestyle and BrainAGE in adult depression.
item.description: This study investigates how heterogeneity in lifestyle and physical fitness shapes patterns of brain ageing in depression. The study sample included medically healthy adults from the UK Biobank (44-82 years) with a history of depression (n = 896) and non-psychiatric controls (n = 36,206). Heterogeneity through Discriminative Analysis (HYDRA) was used to derive data-driven subgroups within the depression sample based on 224 behavioural and physical health features.

item.title: Optimizing Clozapine Use Through Therapeutic Drug Monitoring-Integrating Clinical and Laboratory Science Perspectives.
item.description: Clozapine, a second-generation antipsychotic, remains the most effective pharmacologic option for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, though it remains underutilized due to multiple factors, including patient concerns about adverse effects and limited prescriber familiarity with its optimal use. Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) is highly recommended for clozapine and can support individualized dosing, enhance safety, and improve clinical decision making by providing an objective measure of drug exposure.

item.title: Modifiable psychosocial risk factors for depression among cancer survivors in the United States.
item.description: Depression is highly prevalent among cancer survivors and contributes to poorer quality of life, reduced treatment adherence, and increased morbidity. Functional limitations, loneliness, and inadequate social and emotional support are important psychosocial factors associated with self-reported lifetime diagnosis of major depressive disorder among cancer survivors.

item.title: Enhancing diagnostic and prognostic prediction of child psychopathology via multivariate predictive modeling: Where are we and where do we need to go?
item.description: Advances in computational science and machine learning provide an opportunity to improve access and quality of mental health care in the near-term. Applications of these tools to child dysregulatory psychopathology and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder are of particular interest because they are common and place high burden on healthcare systems; early identification and effective treatment can alter life-long trajectories.

item.title: ADHD symptom positivity and its association with medication adherence and psychiatric burden in adults with epilepsy.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms are increasingly recognized in adults with epilepsy (AwE) and may contribute to psychiatric burden, seizure-related outcomes, and treatment adherence. We therefore investigated the frequency of ADHD symptom positivity and its associations with medication adherence, psychiatric symptoms, seizure burden, and neurophysiological findings. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 100 AwE and 94 healthy controls. ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS-v1.1).

item.title: Ketamine in Modern Medicine: Current Evidence in Acute Pain, Opioid Use Disorder, and Depression.
item.description: Ketamine has continued to be a valuable adjunct in perioperative care, supported by recent meta-analyses demonstrating opioid-sparing effects and improved analgesia, particularly in opioid-tolerant patients and painful surgeries. Its use should be targeted to patients most likely to benefit from its unique properties. Beyond acute pain, ketamine shows promise in patients with opioid use disorder by mitigating tolerance and withdrawal through N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor modulation and downstream neuroadaptive effects.

item.title: Investigating the role of mental health and lifestyle behaviours in the risk of adolescent suicidal behaviours through machine learning.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Suicidal behaviors among adolescents are a serious global public health concern and are closely linked to both mental health and everyday lifestyle behaviors. Suicidal ideation, planning, and attempts lie along a spectrum of increasing severity. However, how psychological distress and health-related behaviors interact to influence suicide risk is complex and not yet fully understood. This study aimed to identify key mental health and lifestyle factors associated with different stages of adolescent suicidal behaviors using interpretable machine learning methods.

item.title: Assessing the effects of supplementation of vitamins on schizophrenia using Mendelian randomization analysis.
item.description: ObjectiveVitamins are essential for human health and the prevention of diseases. They play an important role in maintaining brain function and mental health, especially in patients with schizophrenia. We aimed to evaluate the potential effects of genetic signatures predicting the intake of several vitamins on the risk of schizophrenia.MethodsTwo-sample Mendelian randomization analysis was used to evaluate the potential causal effects of the intake of seven vitamins (vitamins A-E, multivitamins, and folate) on schizophrenia.

item.title: Diagnosis and Management of Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder, Premenstrual Syndrome, and Premenstrual Exacerbation.
item.description: Premenstrual symptoms occur in the late luteal phase as a result of differential sensitivity to normal hormonal fluctuations. These symptoms can include mood symptoms such as mood lability, anxiety, sadness or irritability as well as physical symptoms such as lethargy, bloating and breast tenderness. Symptoms can significantly impact quality of life, particularly in patients with the more severe form of premenstrual symptoms, PMDD. Importantly, symptoms should improve or resolve in the follicular phase.

item.title: When Tics and Autism Meet: Phenomenology, Severity, and Treatment Patterns.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Tic disorders frequently co-occur with neurodevelopmental conditions, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, the impact of ASD on tic phenomenology, severity, and treatment patterns remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: To compare clinical characteristics, tic phenomenology, severity, and treatment patterns in individuals with tic disorders with and without comorbid ASD. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 535 participants from Calgary Child and Adult Tic Disorders Clinical Registries.

item.title: Adolescent attitudes to illicit drug use, education and support: a qualitative study in the United Kingdom.
item.description: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to explore young people's knowledge and attitudes around illicit drug use, its prevention, and the barriers and facilitators to accessing support, with the aim of informing the development of preventative interventions that resonate with young people and address their specific needs and concerns. By drawing on these insights, interventions can be tailored to be more engaging, relevant and impactful for young people.

item.title: National trends in cardiovascular deaths with concurrent accidental drug poisoning coding in the United States: a 22-year analysis of the CDC WONDER database (1999-2020).
item.description: OBJECTIVE: While the overdose epidemic garners significant public health attention, cardiovascular deaths with concurrent accidental drug poisoning coding remain understudied in the United States.Traditional drug mortality surveillance primarily focuses on direct overdose fatalities, with limited integration of modern CDC-aligned multi-cause coding frameworks and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) cardiotoxicity mechanisms.We examined national trends in this phenomenon from 1999 to 2020.

item.title: Lifetime Prevalence of Nonsuicidal Self-Injury in Adolescents: Reliability of a Dichotomous Survey Item.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Nonsuicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a widespread phenomenon among adolescents. Accurate estimates of prevalence rates when screening for NSSI are essential both in research and clinical settings. However, high variability raises the question of the reliability of self-reported NSSI prevalence. METHODS: The reliability of a dichotomous survey item on history of NSSI was investigated longitudinally using data from five time points across 16 months in a community sample (N = 253) of Swedish adolescents (age M = 14.21 years, SD = 0.56, 58.5% female).

item.title: The course and remission of suicidality from ages 11 to 29: findings from a Dutch population-based longitudinal cohort study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Suicide is a leading cause of death among adolescents and emerging adults. Suicidality is a multidimensional construct that includes suicidal ideation (SI), self-harm (SH), suicide attempts, and suicide completion, without a fixed or linear progression between these elements. We examined the course of suicidality (SI/SH) over adolescence and young adulthood (age 11-29) and correlates of natural remission and recovery over these 18 years, using the Dutch population-based longitudinal TRAcking Individuals Lives Survey (TRAILS).

item.title: Perceived satisfaction with care, service atmosphere and mood fluctuations among patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorder in Italian mental health supported accommodations: a multicenter study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Supported Accommodations (SA) are central to Italy's community-based mental health care for individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD), offering structured, recovery-oriented environments. While symptom severity remains important, care environment and satisfaction strongly influence well-being. Mood fluctuations, a key aspect of daily functioning, have been underexplored in SA. Using the Experience Sampling Method (ESM), this study aims to examine the associations between perceived ward atmosphere, care satisfaction, and momentary mood in SA residents with SSD.

item.title: Neurophysiological dynamics related to perception, action, and language in schizophrenia.
item.description: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models.

item.title: Catching the "Pink Flags": Using Smart Devices to Spot Early Signs of Postpartum Psychosis.
item.description: Postpartum psychosis is an underrecognized condition that can have tragic consequences without intervention. In this News and Perspectives article, JMIR Correspondent Benedette Cuffari reports on how technology could support earlier identification and treatment.

item.title: Global organization of structural covariance networks derived from parcellated cortical surface area in atypical populations.
item.description: Higher-order features of brain organization are powerful measures for understanding the relationship between brain and experience. In particular, the global arrangement of structural features of the cortex provides insight into neurodevelopmental processes that underlie individual differences in perception and cognition. Structural covariance networks (SCNs), which capture regional coordination of brain morphometry, are an efficient method to derive global cortical properties.

item.title: Training community providers in prolonged exposure: outcomes of a French consultation programme.
item.description: Background: Prolonged Exposure (PE) is a first-line treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), yet its availability remains limited in France.

item.title: Examining the performance of the International Trauma Questionnaire with clinical checks in a multinational European sample.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The International Trauma Questionnaire (ITQ) is a widely used self-report measure of PTSD and Complex PTSD (CPTSD). 'Clinical checks' - brief follow up questions verifying respondent comprehension of the symptom item - have recently been developed for the ITQ to reduce false-positive diagnostic cases. This study tested whether the ITQ with clinical checks generates psychometrically sound scores and adds clinically relevant information to standard symptom assessment.

item.title: Network analysis of intimate partner violence and depression-anxiety symptoms in Chinese transgender women.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Chinese transgender women have a higher prevalence of intimate partner violence (IPV) compared to their cisgender counterparts. To mitigate the risk of IPV, it is crucial to comprehend the symptoms of emotional distress that are most closely associated with IPV. This network analysis investigated the item-level connections among depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and IPV among Chinese transgender women.

item.title: Association between malaria in pregnancy and children's socio-emotional development at 6 years of Age in Benin: A prospective mother-child cohort.
item.description: BACKGROUND: In 2023, 12.7 million women were exposed to malaria during pregnancy (MiP), mainly in sub-Saharan Africa. MiP is linked to adverse birth outcomes and cognitive deficits in children, but its association with socio-emotional development remains unclear. This study examines associations between MiP-at any time, specific time points, and by infection frequency-and children's socio-emotional development at 6 years. METHODS AND FINDINGS: Data derive from the MiPPAD clinical trial, the nested APEC study, and the EXPLORE follow-up at 6 years.

item.title: Traffic-related air pollution links with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in Denmark: Developmental periods of susceptibility and sex-specificity.
item.description: Literature supports that higher early life exposure to air pollution arising from combustion, e.g., traffic exhaust and electric power generation, is associated with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, little is known about whether certain periods of exposure during fetal or childhood brain development are more important, i.e. whether there are critical windows of exposure, or whether associations differ by child sex. To address these gaps, we performed a population-based case-cohort study including singletons born 1981-2008 using Danish national registry data resources.

item.title: From backlog to blind spots: improving data visibility across autism and ADHD pathways in England.
item.description: All-age autism and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder pathway reform in England is often framed around waiting lists and capacity. However, backlog data alone cannot show how people move through referral, triage, assessment, support and follow-up, or where inequities and unmet need are hidden. Current data also struggle to distinguish confirmed diagnosis, suspected diagnosis, disclosure, self-identification and co-occurring needs. This creates pathway blindness: systems can see pressure, but not flow, fairness or diagnostic visibility.

item.title: RETRACTED: Akter et al. Improved Transfer-Learning-Based Facial Recognition Framework to Detect Autistic Children at an Early Stage. Brain Sci. 2021, 11, 734.
item.description: The journal retracts the article, "Improved Transfer-Learning-Based Facial Recognition Framework to Detect Autistic Children at an Early Stage" [...].

item.title: Bridging language phenotypes, neural dynamics and gene regulation in autism.
item.description: Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASDs) affect approximately 1% of the global population, with prevalence rising over recent decades. Although ASDs are heritable (~70%), translating genetic findings into effective therapeutics remains challenging due to the vast number of implicated risk genes (>700) and the limited influence of individual genes on disease expression. Their collective impact and convergent expression patterns of small-effect genes provide insights into ASD-related neurobiological mechanisms.

item.title: KATNAL2 dysfunction impairs microtubule dynamics and contributes to syndromic neurodevelopmental disease.
item.description: Katanins are microtubule-severing ATPases. Dysfunction of katanin subunits has been implicated in impaired neurogenesis, morphogenesis, and neuronal migration. Although heterozygous variants in KATNAL2 (katanin-like 2), a known autism-spectrum disorder (ASD) risk gene, have been reported in patients with ASD or other neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD), the underlying cellular mechanisms remain incompletely defined.
